input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position. Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables (20.1) and for Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2). Standard procedure (prompt notice, cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense, control of defence, prejudice-limited notice failure, settlement consent) appears in 20.4, and 20.5 adds the procure/modify/replace/refund remedy at Vendor's expense in addition to defence. Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow (unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized, and Customer's violation of Applicable Law), with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications and combinations. Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under 21.3, so the Vendor indemnity is not squeezed by the liability cap — better than the fallback super-cap. No redline required.
